en: The *Śatasahasramudrā-dhāraṇī-sūtra*, one fascicle.
Translated by the Tripitaka Master Śikṣānanda of the Great Zhou, by imperial decree.
Thus have I heard. At one time, the Buddha was staying at Vulture Peak Mountain in the city of Rājagṛha, together with a great [assembly].
Together with the assembly of bhikṣus and the great assembly of bodhisattvas,
the World-Honored One then addressed the bhikṣus:
"There is a dhāraṇī named 'Hundred Thousand Seals.'"
You all should receive and uphold this:
namely, take refuge in the Tathāgata Suvarṇaprabhāsa-uttaptaketurāja-viśālavadanamauliprasphoṭita;
take refuge in the Tathāgata Śākyamuni, the Arhat, the Samyaksaṃbuddha.
Then he spoke the root dhāraṇī, saying:
Tadyathā | Oṃ | Bhu bhu bhu bhu bhu | Sarvatathāgata-vajra | Dhara dhara | Hara hara | Vahara vahara.

This is the root dhāraṇī.
Oṃ sarvatathāgatavijaye jaya jaya svāhā. This is the heart-mantra (*hṛdaya-mantra*) of the dhāraṇī.
Oṃ hulu hulu jayamukha svāhā. This is the subsidiary heart-mantra (*upahṛdaya-mantra*).
If there are bhikṣus, bhikṣuṇīs, upāsakas, upāsikās,
or other sons and daughters of good family with pure faith who are able to construct a stūpa and inscribe this *Śatasahasramudrā-dhāraṇī* within it;
The merit obtained from constructing this single stūpa is no different from the merit of constructing one hundred thousand stūpas.
After the Buddha had spoken this sūtra, [he sat in silence].
Those bhikṣus and the assembly of bodhisattvas,
along with the devas, humans, asuras, and others,
having heard what the Buddha had spoken, were all greatly rejoiced; they believed, accepted, and practiced it accordingly.
The Dhāraṇī Sūtra of One Hundred Thousand Seals (Śatasahasramudrā-dhāraṇī-sūtra)
